caption: Real arguments use the analytic continuation $2^{(1+2x-\cos\pi x)/4}\,\pi^{(\cos\pi x-1)/4}\,\Gamma(1+\frac{x}{2})$
sage.note: Sage raises TypeError: Attempt to coerce non-integral RealNumber to Integer; ours answers 2.407069456116044.
sympy.note: SymPy's factorial2 takes a nonnegative or negative odd integer only; ours continues it analytically to a real argument.
mathlib4.note: Ours evaluates a non-integer argument (exactly or through Gamma); Mathlib's Nat.doubleFactorial takes natural numbers, so it does not typecheck.
julia.note: Combinatorics.jl's Factorial2 counts take an integer only; compute-engine extends it past the integers.

caption: The number of ways to pair up 10 people into 5 couples: $(2n-1)!!$ counts perfect matchings of $2n$ objects
Splits an ordinary factorial into even and odd parts: $n! = n!!\,(n-1)!!$
Negative even arguments hit a pole in the recurrence, so compute-engine returns ComplexInfinity
sage.note: Both decline: Sage raises ValueError: multifactorial undefined; ours leaves ComplexInfinity.
sympy.note: Both decline at the pole: ours answers ComplexInfinity, SymPy's factorial2 raises a ValueError at a negative even integer.
mpmath.note: Both decline: ours answers ComplexInfinity, mpmath raises ValueError.
mathlib4.note: A negative argument is outside Mathlib's natural-number domain, so Nat.doubleFactorial does not typecheck; ours answers ComplexInfinity (a pole).
julia.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers ComplexInfinity, Julia raises an error (DomainError with -2: n must be nonnegati).
